summary: Three generated functions are SECURITY DEFINER (_delta_holders, _delta_serial_new, _delta_serial_past), so their generated predicates are the only guard there
detail: Any compiler bug in a permission check is a data leak, as October showed. The handover's direction for delta: run compiled functions as the invoker under FORCE RLS so row-level security is the backstop. Decide whether dzql adopts that or the path compiler moves to delta.
note: 2026-10-16: the path compiler moved to delta (owns as a path, compiled per document, a row never handed away). Derived RLS is still to do: probed, PGlite enforces RLS for a NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS role, so it can be tested without a server; but the fan-out (holders, told) reads other documents' rows inside the writer's transaction, so invoker functions under FORCE RLS need policies that let it, or the fan-out runs as the owner. Its own piece of work.

summary: A schema per app on one database is not supported: the change channel is database-wide
detail: With the framework retired (todo #26), one generateSql serves one app's definitions, so two apps on one Postgres server each need a database of their own (CREATE DATABASE; LISTEN/NOTIFY is per database). Peter asked (2026-10-16) whether Postgres schemas could separate apps within one database instead: lighter to administer. They could: each app's _delta_* tables, ledger, dispatchers and compiled functions live in its schema, and the SECURITY DEFINER functions already pin the search path they were applied with. Missing: the pool's search_path set to the app's schema (applyFramework, applySql, createDocListener), and NOTIFY on a channel named for the schema (delta_changes is database-wide, so each app would hear the other's names; harmless to the subscribers, but a custom document reads each one). Wants a test with two apps in two schemas of one database, each writing, undoing and told only its own.
note: 2026-10-20: fixed: namespace on openStore, openDatabase, applyFramework, applySql and createDocListener keeps an app in a Postgres schema of its own, made when missing; 001c tells its changes on _delta_channel() (delta:<schema>; public keeps delta_changes) and keys a listener's lock by the schema; PGlite gives each query its pool's path. tests/delta-pg/namespaces.test.ts: two apps of one table and document name, on one PGlite and on the server through openStore, each writing, undoing and told only its own; docs/postgres/postgres.md, Several apps on one database

summary: A page cannot read a ref's row as it stood: the cafe's orders still copy the dish's name and price
detail: Decided (#52): an order names its dish (dish: menu:/items) and says ordered_at, and reads the dish and its price as they stood then, rather than copying them. A page is drawn synchronously from the documents the kernel holds (src/rendering/documents.ts), and a dish taken off the menu is a closed version no held document has; open_at is a call, not a held read. The seam: the kernel holds a ref's rows as they stood (a document of the referenced collection's versions, or open_at held per time), read as any document is. Then the cafe's model changes (orders: dish, ordered_at; a migration), its table resource writes the ref, and the floor and the table read the dish through it.
